title: Empowering Electron Ptychography with Generative Artificial Intelligence and Agentic Workflows
content: Generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly foundation models such as Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs), is rapidly transforming scientific research by enabling unprecedented levels of automation. Trained on extensive text and image data, these models effectively capture advanced domain knowledge and excel at natural-language-based tasks ranging from text summarization to image interpretation. Advanced reasoning models with mathematical problem-solving and self-correcting capabilities show great potential for deriving sophisticated scientific insights and inspiring new ideas. However, harnessing their full capabilities in scientific applications often requires carefully designed workflows to ensure accuracy, reproducibility, and robustness. One promising strategy is the use of agentic or multi-agent frameworks, where specialized AI agents independently handle subtasks such as information retrieval, code generation, or quality assessment, thus reducing errors and improving reliability. In this talk, I will discuss how agentic workflows and reasoning LLMs can facilitate autonomous experimental controls, data analysis, and research in electron ptychography.
